claims.description: A 24-hour-format time string (e.g. "22:00") is parsed to minutes since midnight, so the closing time extracted from a 24-hour range like "10:00-22:00" is surfaced as that time.
claims.commentRef: L12 * Parse time string like "10:00 PM" or "22:00" to minutes since midnight ; L17 // Handle 24-hour format (e.g., "22:00")

claims.description: A 12-hour-format time string (e.g. "10:00 PM") is parsed to minutes since midnight: PM adds 12 hours except at 12 PM, and 12 AM is midnight.
The closing time is extracted from the documented opening-hours range formats: "10:00 AM - 10:00 PM" and "10:00-22:00".
claims.commentRef: L42-46 * Parse opening hours string and extract closing time / * Handles formats like: / * - "10:00 AM - 10:00 PM" / * - "10:00-22:00" / * - "Open 24 hours" ; L57 // Format: "HH:MM AM - HH:MM PM" or "HH:MM - HH:MM"

claims.description: A place whose opening hours say it is open 24 hours is never reported as closing soon (it never has a closing time).
claims.commentRef: L51 // Check for 24 hours ; L53 return null; // Open 24 hours, never closing

claims.description: A closing time that falls after midnight relative to the current time (e.g. closes 1:00 AM while it is late evening) is handled by treating it as tomorrow, yielding a positive minutes-until-close.
claims.commentRef: L93 // Handle cases where closing time is after midnight (e.g., 1:00 AM) ; L96 // Closing time might be tomorrow (past midnight)

claims.description: When more than 12 hours remain until the computed closing time, the place is treated as already closed from yesterday rather than closing soon.
claims.commentRef: L100 // If more than 12 hours until close, it's probably already closed from yesterday

claims.description: formatTimeUntilClose renders minutes-until-close as a human-readable string: "Closing now" at or below zero, "Closes in N min" under an hour, and "Closes in Hh" / "Closes in Hh Mm" at or above an hour.
claims.commentRef: L113 * Format minutes until close into a human-readable string

claims.description: calculateDistance returns the great-circle distance between two latitude/longitude points in kilometers, computed with the Haversine formula using Earth's radius of 6371 km.
claims.commentRef: L2 * Calculate distance between two coordinates using the Haversine formula ; L7 * @returns Distance in kilometers ; L15 const R = 6371; // Earth's radius in kilometers

claims.description: formatDistance renders a distance in kilometers as a display string: distances under 1 km as whole meters ("500 m", km*1000 rounded), and 1 km or more as one-decimal kilometers ("1.2 km").
claims.commentRef: L34 * Format distance for display ; L36 * @returns Formatted string (e.g., "1.2 km" or "500 m")

claims.description: getCategoriesForMood returns exactly the category list configured for the given mood in moodConfigs (and an empty array when no config matches); getMoodConfig finds the config whose id equals the requested mood.
claims.commentRef: L21 categories: ['cafe', 'coffee_shop'], // Cafes for work ; L29 // Restaurants, cafes, bars for dates ; L37 // Fast food and quick spots ; L45 // Budget-friendly places ; L53 // Chill cafes and bars ; L61 // Bars and party spots

claims.description: The category id strings in each mood config are valid Foursquare category IDs (the mapping documented at the Foursquare categories docs URL).

unverifiable.reason: Whether each string is a valid Foursquare category ID can only be confirmed against the external Foursquare categories API/taxonomy; the mapping is consumed by the network-backed places service, so there is no deterministic, network-free way to execute this claim (R3.6).
